recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow source correction to an active datatype examples page, restores the previously applied Jira decision, and keeps the later JSON examples consistent with the corrected XML examples.
issue_request: FHIR-20670 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes technical correction noting that the Timing example snippets used root nodes named <schedule> rather than <timing>; the Jira comment said this was not technically wrong but would be less confusing if fixed.
initial_application: Commit b1a191ea63c373039d54c387aced8a9f11daea24 initially applied FHIR-20670 by changing the Timing XML examples from schedule roots to timing roots. The next-day RatioRange datatype commit b9fd58139d35c8aa90083ae99a279c8a6d3dd854 reintroduced schedule roots while editing the same page, leaving the current combined branch without the Jira-tagged fix.
additional_context: Timing remains an active datatype in source/fhir.ini, and source/datatypes-examples.html is the active datatype examples source. Later commit e9e4e5f34c8d0b40d680c26f92acfa19b5f714a6 added JSON examples after the XML roots had regressed, so the same root-name correction applies to the JSON fragments. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Edited source/datatypes-examples.html so all six Timing XML snippets use <timing>...</timing> roots and all six corresponding JSON snippets use "timing" as the root property.
source_changes: source/datatypes-examples.html: changed six Timing XML example roots from <schedule>...</schedule> to <timing>...</timing> and six corresponding JSON root properties from "schedule" to "timing".

related_jiras.note: A later datatype examples commit added JSON fragments after the Timing roots had regressed, which made it necessary to apply the same FHIR-20670 naming correction to the JSON roots; no separate decision was made for FHIR-19608.
